issues.legal_issue: For a final partition decree that has determined the parties’ rights and is not contingent on a further event, the execution limitation period begins when the decree is pronounced, even if the decree-holder has not yet supplied stamp paper needed to engross it.
material_facts: A final partition decree determining the parties’ shares was pronounced after the commissioner’s report was accepted.
The decree-holder was notified to provide stamp paper but did not do so; providing it was within the decree-holder’s control.
The decree contained no condition requiring a further event or adjudication before it could be enforced.
The decree-holder’s legal representatives filed an execution application more than twelve years after the decree was pronounced.
issues.conclusion: The decree became enforceable when pronounced, and the execution application filed more than twelve years later was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963, starts the twelve-year period when a decree becomes enforceable. ‘Enforceable’ is to be given its literal meaning; enforceability is distinct from executability. A decree that finally determines rights and is not conditional is enforceable when pronounced, even if a ministerial step such as supplying stamp paper remains. A decree-holder cannot suspend limitation through failure to perform an act within their control. This applies the approach in Yeswant Deorao Deshmukh v. Walchand Ramchand Kothari, W.B. Essential Commodities Supply Corporation v. Swadesh Agro Farming & Storage Pvt. Ltd., Biswapati Dey v. Kennsington Stores, and Subhash Ganpatrao Buty v. Maroti Krishnaji Dorlikar. Shankar Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shankar Lokhande concerned a different situation in which no final decree had been passed and does not govern this case.

predicates.final_partition_decree_pronounced: The court pronounced a final decree partitioning property.
predicates.rights_fully_determined: The decree conclusively determined the parties’ rights without leaving those rights for later adjudication.
predicates.no_contingent_event_or_further_adjudicat: The decree did not make enforcement dependent on an external event or a further determination by the court.

issues.definition: When an execution application concerns a final partition decree that determines the parties’ rights, has no remaining contingency or adjudication, and requires only stamp paper within the decree-holder’s control, an application filed after the limitation period has elapsed is barred.

issues.legal_issue: The stamp-law restrictions on receiving or acting upon an unstamped instrument do not suspend the limitation period for execution of a final partition decree.
material_facts: The final partition decree had been pronounced and had crystallised the parties’ rights.
The decree-holder had not supplied stamp paper needed to engross the decree, although doing so was within the decree-holder’s control.
The execution application was filed more than twelve years after the decree was pronounced.
The decree-holder argued that the stamp-law restrictions prevented the decree from being enforceable until it was engrossed on stamp paper.
issues.conclusion: The stamp-law provisions do not suspend limitation; the execution application was barred because the limitation period ran from the date the decree became enforceable.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(15) and 35 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899, address the status and use of an instrument that is not duly stamped; they do not govern when limitation for execution begins. Article 136 of the Limitation Act, 1963, operates in a distinct sphere, and the stamp-law restrictions do not suspend its limitation period. The Court rejected the contrary view in Bholanath Karmakar v. Madanmohan Karmakar. It distinguished Shankar Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shankar Lokhande, which involved the absence of a final decree, and relied on the distinction between enforceability and executability explained in the judgment.

issues.definition: When execution of a pronounced final partition decree is sought while a stamp-related formality within the decree-holder’s control remains outstanding, that formality does not suspend limitation, and an application filed after the limitation period has elapsed is barred.
